Chapter 02 of 19

Morning Mist

citywide from Trout Lake
The story

When the meeting ends, the city has to be told what it needs. Nobody sends a message. Instead, a light mist, or a thin rain, drifts out of Trout Lake and settles over every district before sunrise, catching on telephone wires, wet paint, rails, glass, seawall lamps and tree branches.

The mist does not carry instructions. It carries a state: where things are urgent, where a boundary has gone weak, where sound and colour are thinning. Every part of the city reads the same mist differently. A Repair Person feels where to patch. The wires feel where a song should land. A boundary feels where to hold. Nothing is written in the air, but unrelated things wake up and change their tone together.

That is how you spot it. Not by the weather, which looks like ordinary Vancouver weather, but by the way the city seems to agree with itself all at once. The mist carries what is needed, not how to do it.

Terminal City is an original fictional mythology inspired by Vancouver’s geography, weather, wildlife, infrastructure, art, and electronic music. It makes no claim to historical, Indigenous, or religious tradition. Real places are used as settings; the operating system layered on them is invented. Photograph reality. Alter the evidence. Never illustrate the whole myth.
